messages.author: 5ce86f6dabf3a413
messages.subject: Measurement invariance with three groups
parts:
Dear all, 
I am relatively new to lavaan and SEM, and I would like to ask you for some advice. I am trying to evaluate measurement invariance of an instrument (four factor, 22 continuous items) across three different groups. My doubts are as follows:

1. Following the lavaan tutorial, with equality constraints in place for factor loadings and item intercepts, I am fixing the latent mean of each factor to zero in the first group (G1, reference group), whereas these means are freely estimated in the other two groups (G2 and G3). Can I interpret the latent means of G2 and G3 in each factor as differences between G2 vs G1, and G3 vs G1, respectively, as in the case of an analysis with two groups?

2. How about a post-hoc analysis of latent mean differences between G2 and G3?

3. I have some missing values. Is it possible to use full-information maximum likelihood together with the MLR estimator in the framework of measurement invariance?

Thank you very much for your help.

All the best

Marika

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Measurement invariance with three groups
parts: 1. Following the lavaan tutorial, with equality constraints in place for factor loadings and item intercepts, I am fixing the latent mean of each factor to zero in the first group (G1, reference group), whereas these means are freely estimated in the other two groups (G2 and G3). Can I interpret the latent means of G2 and G3 in each factor as differences between G2 vs G1, and G3 vs G1, respectively, as in the case of an analysis with two groups?

####
For this to hold you need to achieve strong measurement invariance, meaning that both factor loadings and indicator intercepts can be equated between groups.
Once you have achieve this, yes, the means for g2 and g3 would be the difference with respect of G1, because its set to 0
You can also use the function measEq.syntax() from the semTools package to create the models syntax for these steps, in case you are not clear

####
2. How about a post-hoc analysis of latent mean differences between G2 and G3?

####
If you want to use the wlad test, you can label the factor means, and create define parameters for the mean differences, like this

factor1 ~c(0, NA, NA)*1 + c(m1g1, m1g2, m1g3)*1

m1g23 := m1g2 - m1g3

This new parameter m1g23 will test the hypothesis of mean G2 being equal to mean G3. Would need to write this up for each factor

####
3. I have some missing values. Is it possible to use full-information maximum likelihood together with the MLR estimator in the framework of measurement invariance?

####
Yes, as long as you use a ML type estimator, such as MLR. Add the arguments estimator="MLR", missing="fiml"

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Measurement invariance with three groups
parts:
Marika

I dont know a paper that specifically talks about this mean difference, because there is no dispute about it.

The mean of G2 and G3 are not by definition the difference with respect of G1. Their means are estimated with G1 as the point of reference. They represent the difference because G1 is fix at 0, you could fix it 10 if you want and G2 and G3 would change accordingly, in refernece to it

Even when G2 and G3 are the difference with G1, the effect of G1 "cancels out" when comparing G2 and G3. Because if both have G1 as the same reference point, their difference (G2 - G3) is still the difference that is not related to the difference with G1. Think like you are adding a constant to both sides of the substraction, the final substraction will result in the same (G2-0) - (G3-0)

Hope this helps
